artifacts.description: Time-domain HRV indices (RMSSD, MeanNN, etc.) for the resting 5-min ECG recording.
artifacts.source_evidence: The narrative section 'Time-Domain Analysis' interprets these features in their own right (RMSSD, MeanNN, ...). Produced by 'hrv_time = nk.hrv_time(peaks, sampling_rate=100, show=True)' and still held in 'hrv_time' at completion.

artifacts.description: Frequency-domain HRV spectral power indices across frequency bands.
artifacts.source_evidence: The narrative section 'Frequency-Domain Analysis' extracts and interprets spectral power density per band. Produced by 'hrv_freq = nk.hrv_frequency(peaks, sampling_rate=100, show=True, normalize=True)' and still held in 'hrv_freq' at completion.

artifacts.description: Non-linear domain HRV indices (Poincaré SD1/SD2, entropy and related measures).
artifacts.source_evidence: The narrative section 'Non-Linear Domain Analysis' computes and discusses the non-linear indices from hrv_nonlinear(). Produced by 'hrv_nonlinear = nk.hrv_nonlinear(peaks, sampling_rate=100, show=True)' and still held in 'hrv_nonlinear' at completion.

artifacts.description: Combined HRV indices across all three domains for the same R-peak series.
artifacts.source_evidence: The final section 'All Domains' presents the consolidated result: 'hrv_indices = nk.hrv(peaks, sampling_rate=100, show=True)'. It is the source's culminating end product and persists in 'hrv_indices' at completion.

excluded_outputs: Raw signal data (ECG, PPG, RSP) loaded via nk.data('bio_resting_5min_100hz') — source inputs for the analysis, not scientific outcomes of it.
peaks signal DataFrame and info dict from nk.ecg_peaks — intermediates preparing the R-peak series consumed by the HRV functions; the narrative does not interpret them as independent results.

Plots generated by show=True in hrv_time, hrv_frequency, hrv_nonlinear and hrv (RR-interval distribution, power spectral density, Poincaré scattergram) — visualizations whose underlying numeric content exists either inside the plotting functions or is already captured in the exported HRV index tables; no figure capture is added and no plot-only values are reconstructed.
plan.explanation: The notebook's terminal scientific products are the HRV indices tables themselves, which the narrative interprets in each domain (time, frequency, non-linear) plus the combined all-domains result. All four DataFrames (hrv_time, hrv_freq, hrv_nonlinear, hrv_indices) persist unmodified at script completion, so the appended code only writes each stored table to CSV with its own pandas writer, preserving column labels (the index names) and row ordering. Plots and peak detection are excluded as visual/intermediate material.
plan.export_code:
import os

os.makedirs("/work/outputs", exist_ok=True)

hrv_time.to_csv("/work/outputs/hrv_time.csv", index=False)
hrv_freq.to_csv("/work/outputs/hrv_freq.csv", index=False)
hrv_nonlinear.to_csv("/work/outputs/hrv_nonlinear.csv", index=False)
hrv_indices.to_csv("/work/outputs/hrv_indices.csv", index=False)
unresolved_assumptions: Assumes the four HRV result DataFrames hold a single row of named metric columns as returned by NeuroKit2 at the source revision; actual column sets and any NaN entries are only verifiable at execution.
Assumes neurokit2 and its plotting backends (matplotlib, underlying scipy) import and run within the offline CPU-only limits; dependency resolution is an execution-stage concern.
